# Attestation Policy

- **CURIE:** [`gmeow:AttestationPolicy`](gmeow-AttestationPolicy.md)
- **IRI:** <https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/AttestationPolicy>
- **Category:** class
- **Defined by:** [`gmeow:slices/attestation`](../../slices/attestation.md)
- **Box roles:** [CBox role](../boxes/cbox.md), [TBox role](../boxes/tbox.md) ([What is this?](../../four-boxes/index.md))

The policy or framework under which an attestation was issued — a value vocabulary (individuals, never subclasses). Open-ended; specific policies are minted as needed.

## Structure

**Subclass of:** [`gufo:QualityValue`](../../external/terms.md#gufo-qualityvalue)

## Practical Pattern

Use [`gmeow:AttestationPolicy`](gmeow-AttestationPolicy.md) as a specialized kind of [`gufo:QualityValue`](../../external/terms.md#gufo-qualityvalue). Add statement metadata or a standpoint when the assertion needs provenance, confidence, or vantage.

## Usage Advice

### Use when

- Use as the value vocabulary behind [`gmeow:attestationPolicy`](../properties/gmeow-attestationPolicy.md) — the open set of individuals naming the rules or framework an attester followed (a SLSA build level, a credential-issuance policy, an editorial standard).

### Avoid when

- Avoid minting per-policy subclasses (policies are individuals) and avoid using it for the attestation kind ([`gmeow:AttestationType`](gmeow-AttestationType.md)); the policy is the governing framework, not the category, and policy satisfaction is a solver-layer verdict.

### How to use

- Mint each policy as an individual and reference it via [`gmeow:attestationPolicy`](../properties/gmeow-attestationPolicy.md); the determination of whether a policy was met is a [`gmeow:VerificationResult`](gmeow-VerificationResult.md) (status policy-failed when unmet), computed in the solver layer.

### Examples

- ex:slsaL3 a [`gmeow:AttestationPolicy`](gmeow-AttestationPolicy.md); [rdfs:label](http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#label) "SLSA build level 3"@en.
